review_type: single AI curator; full received final answer read; model identity visible

errors.quote: compare against the full-n estimate treated as a reference
errors.issue: The subsample is included in the full-n reference, creating correlated estimation errors. Use disjoint reference samples or quantify this dependence rather than treating agreement as independent recovery.

errors.quote: Held-out replicates:** where n ≥ 4 per condition, estimate on a 2-vs-2 subsample and test recovery of the full-data calls
errors.issue: These full-data calls are not held out. A no-tuning rule does not remove shared observations between the estimate and its validation target.

Protein abundance and RNA abundance are different estimands. Protein disagreement may reflect translation or degradation biology rather than inaccurate RNA fold changes; it is not interchangeable magnitude ground truth.

The table restricts this to low-count effects lacking coherent biology and expects shrinkage to suppress them. Batch artifacts can be precise, high-count and pathway-coherent; shrinkage is not a general confounding correction.

errors.quote: base mean below the filter threshold
errors.issue: The primary pipeline has already filtered on cumulative counts, while this criterion compares a normalized mean to that threshold. Define consistent units and retain a separately evaluated low-information universe; otherwise the purported safeguard can omit the cases it must test.

Extreme observed estimates are not a replacement for independently supported true/reference strong effects. This alternative definition can select the noise that the evaluation is supposed to distinguish.

errors.quote: the packet's count model with cross-gene dispersion shrinkage and a Normal prior
errors.issue: Likelihood, normalization, prior-scale fitting and posterior uncertainty/convergence rules are not operationally specified. A later optional adaptive-prior comparison is also undeveloped.

rationale: Useful provenance and broad simulation structure, but shared-data references are mislabeled held out, validation mixes RNA and protein estimands, and information strata can be circular or filtered away. Technical-artifact assumptions and method specification require substantial correction. No complete adaptive-tail historical intervention is proposed.
reference_guardrails: All four complete final answers in this file, the exact question/packet and full reference were personally read. The long Qwen answer was read in overlapping sections. No paid judge, hidden reasoning or raw-data execution was used.

The packet supplies a generic count model and Normal effect prior; it does not explicitly supply a NB likelihood, a dataset, a calendar cutoff or biological facts. Proposed NB, numerical grids and development thresholds are legitimate when labeled; do not demand invented accession IDs or future-paper names.

Separate scientific proposal quality from strict five-component historical matching. A coherent alternative can score highly without reproducing the later adaptive heavy-tailed intervention. A finite Normal mixture has Gaussian asymptotic tails; it is a related flexible-scale direction, not literally a heavy-tailed distribution.

The key itself leaves algorithm tolerances, datasets and prior fitting unresolved. Apply the operational-detail criterion consistently rather than treating the draft as an executed or complete protocol. A missing source audit is a limitation, not evidence of fabricated data.

More flexible nested models can have worse finite-sample predictive risk. Correct-prior Bayes optimality does not mean zero conditional bias at each effect size. Prior fitting and dispersion estimation must use only the allowed training/small-sample data.

Coefficient information depends on both groups, dispersion and design; count abundance alone is not sufficient. In the standard NB log link, weights involve mu/(1+phi*mu). Keep natural-log and log2 effect scales explicit.

Reference estimates are uncertain. Reusing observations, selecting reference extremes and treating correlated splits as independent can bias evaluation. Same-sample orthogonal assays check measurement agreement; new biological units test biological reproducibility.

Define false-sign events, selected-set versus per-gene denominators, interval coverage and false strong-effect calls separately. Protein effects do not constitute interchangeable ground truth for RNA effects. Ranking or visually smooth plots do not establish uncertainty calibration.

Historical matching is retrospective and not a novelty test. The later journal article is verified; earliest-public-disclosure and full supplement/code audits remain incomplete. Original candidate records and frozen references are preserved.

review_sources.title: Zhu, Ibrahim and Love: Heavy-tailed prior distributions for sequence count data
review_sources.scope: Read primary abstract, introduction and model/prior methods through scale adaptation and MAP computation. These establish the adaptive Cauchy/NB historical direction and the natural-log coefficient scale. No full supplement, code execution or numerical reproduction audit.

mechanism.quote: a Normal prior is misspecified and could bias large true effects toward zero

intervention.quote: a different shrinkage family (e.g., a mixture/adaptive-shrinkage approach)
intervention.assessment: Only an optional family name, without a defined adaptive heavy-tailed model or algorithm.

readout.assessment: Magnitude/ranking endpoints exist, but explicit posterior sign/interval calibration for the new estimator is missing.
